summary: A Network Host Status report from Ellen Westheimer of BBN covering March 27 to April 7, 1972. During this time the Ames PDP-10 acting as front end to the Illiac became a server, though not for general use for months. A terminal IMP was installed at the University of Southern California on March 29. It updates RFC 326.

eli5.summary: This is like a school attendance sheet for the early internet. Someone wrote down which big computers were switched on and ready to help, and which ones were not, so people knew where to go.

subtitle: The next ARPANET host status snapshot, covering 27 March to 7 April 1972.

tldr.problem: Network users needed an up-to-date view of which hosts were available as servers and which were only for users.
tldr.mechanism: BBN again tested hosts daily from its Terminal IMP, recording results as O, H, D, T or R, and listed each site's status or prediction.
tldr.outcome: It is a dated snapshot. The index lists it as obsoleting RFC 326 and as updated by RFC 332.

sections.title: What Changed This Period
sections.content:
This RFC from Ellen Westheimer of BBN reports on the status of most Network Hosts from March 27 to April 7, 1972. The PDP-10 at Ames, which acts as a front-end to the Illiac (Network address 15), became a server, although it will not be available for general use for several months. A Terminal IMP was installed at the University of Southern California (Network address 23) on March 29.

The header says it updates RFC 326 and obsoletes none.
sections.eli5: Two things were new: one more computer started helping, and a new terminal box was plugged in at a university.

sections.title: Hosts Left Out of Daily Testing
sections.content:
Some hosts are excluded from the daily testing. The first group is not expected to be working as servers on a regular basis for at least two weeks: MIT-AI (134) and Case (13). The second group is users only: the Terminal IMPs (AMES, MITRE, NBS, ETAC, USC and BBN), the Network Control Center computer (address 5) used solely for gathering statistics, and Rand (7), Harvard (73), Illinois (12) and NBS (19).

The BBN Terminal IMP (address 158) is a prototype and is often not connected because it is used to refine and debug Terminal IMP programs.
sections.eli5: Some computers were skipped in the daily check because they were not ready, or were only meant for visitors to use.

sections.title: Test Results and Predictions
sections.content:
The results table covers ten test dates from 3/27 to 4/7. The codes are the same as in the previous report: O open, H half open, D dead, T timed out after 60 seconds and R refused. Sites flagged with a hash sign advertise that their system may not be available at that time.

A second table gives each site's status or prediction, such as Server, User Only or "Soon", with the person it came from. As before, the UCLA IBM-360/91 offered only NETRJS, with Telnet expected in April, and the BBN setup could not test it.
sections.eli5: Each day each computer got a one-letter grade, and a second list says which ones promise to be ready soon.
